assets.name: 高空俯视
assets.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural / architectural visualization. A coherent four-view concept series of ONE Chinese mountain wellness resort named 若水汇康养山庄, a high-end but intimate Jiangnan retreat near Hangzhou. This is a proposed resort design, make convincing architectural photography, no website UI, collage, diagram or presentation layout. Brand character: understated ink-landscape elegance, warm ivory, subdued blue-grey, natural tea-green. Architecture identity to preserve in every view: low-rise one/two-storey contemporary Jiangnan buildings with straight shallow-pitched dark grey zinc/tile gable roofs and generous eaves, warm pale limestone/plaster walls, honey-toned timber slat screens, slim dark bronze frames and floor-to-ceiling glass; fine stone paving, clean restrained details. Natural landscape: forested rolling bamboo/tea-covered hills, quiet emerald water, mist-softened distant ridges, native planting. Designed for quiet restorative stays, broadly accessible paths, no fantastical megastructures, no generic white tropical villas, no ornate palace, no dramatic medical equipment, no watermarks or overlay headings. Restrained photorealism with material detail, plausible scale and natural atmosphere, sophisticated editorial hospitality photography. Landscape 16:9 composition, ideally 2048x1152, one full-bleed image.
VIEW 1: HIGH DRONE AERIAL MASTER VIEW. A true high-altitude oblique bird's-eye view from roughly 150 metres above the valley, angled down 55 degrees, showing the whole cohesive resort site and its relation to wooded hills and a small natural reservoir, with complete resort buildings clearly visible. Site layout: at lower-left a modest road and landscaped arrival loop lead to a two-storey central reception/lobby pavilion; behind the lobby two clusters of low-rise guest wings step gently up the wooded slope around small planted courtyards; to the right of lobby, toward the reservoir, a lower single-storey spa pavilion connects to a protected outdoor stone bathing courtyard with two modest rectangular pools and a sheltered timber terrace. A long shallow reflection water garden is the visual axis from entry toward the lobby, distinct from the bathing courtyard. Stone walking paths link buildings, car park screened discreetly at the forest edge, no highway or urban skyline. Leave natural forest between the clusters; built footprint moderate and believable, no endless repetitive villas. Early morning soft warm light from upper-left, very light distant valley mist; immediate architecture remains sharp. Do not show an eye-level exterior perspective: clearly HIGH AERIAL, a land-and-building overview. No signage readable at this altitude, no added labels.

Eye-level frontal three-quarter view from across the entry reflecting pool, 28mm architectural camera, verticals straight. Show the full entrance pavilion and its arrival setting, not a close-up sign. No people crowd, no cars obscuring architecture, no giant lettering, no UI. One landscape image 16:9.

VIEW 3: MAIN LOBBY INTERIOR. Wide but natural 24mm architectural interior photograph at eye level, straight verticals, showing a double-height arrival hall with exposed honey-coloured timber pitched ceiling and slender timber/bronze columns. A long low rounded-corner pale limestone reception desk occupies the left-middle ground; behind it a warm ivory wall with a modest accurate blue-grey emblem and the Chinese brand 若水汇 above the smaller name 康养山庄, physically installed signage, not a text overlay. Full-height glazing opens onto the same calm reflecting garden, bamboo and wooded hillside; deep grey roof eaves visible outside. Pale matte limestone flooring, woven natural textiles, restrained warm indirect light, extensive soft daylight, tactile material detail, elegant ink-landscape framed art only if subtle. Maintain generous level circulation space and an inviting intimate scale, not a shopping mall or ceremonial palace. No crowded guests; keep the architectural space calm and readable. VIEW 4: SPA / HYDROTHERAPY AREA. Image 2 is the approved lobby interior and establishes the exact pale limestone, honey timber pitched ceiling, slatted screens, bronze framing and warm natural lighting. Eye-level wide architectural photograph taken from beneath the spa pavilion's timber ceiling, looking through a broad open glazed wall across a tranquil hydrotherapy pool and toward its landscaped courtyard and the same calm wooded reservoir. Foreground left: a modest pale blue-green hydrotherapy basin with clearly visible gentle bubble jets and two submerged contoured stone relaxation seats; rounded safe pool edge, broad stone coping, discreet stainless handrail and a shallow entry stair. Beyond, a smaller quiet rectangular soaking pool and native planting are visible in the screened courtyard, consistent with the aerial layout. Pool water remains calm apart from localized soft hydrotherapy bubbles, fine restrained steam at the edge only. On the dry right-hand side is a timber lounge deck with three oatmeal fabric reclining beds, neatly rolled white towels, small side tables, and behind a wood slat privacy screen a single quiet treatment alcove with one linen-covered massage bed, naturally integrated and not foreground. Dry circulation routes generous and clearly separated from pools. Warm low-level cove light under timber eaves, diffuse early morning daylight, subtle tactile stone surfaces with realistic water reflections, bamboo and natural rocks outside. No people, no swimwear models, no clinical equipment, no fantasy floating platforms, no decorative indoor waterfall, no excessive smoke, no large signage, no text overlays, no UI. This must read as a restorative spa/hydrotherapy space rather than a generic lap pool or waterpark. Single full-bleed landscape 16:9 photograph.
